Operational Recommendations (Response to 10 % Cost Spike on Sunflower Oil & Basmati Rice)**

column3: **Secure a Multi‑Year Fixed‑Price Contract with a Primary Supplier (or Hedge)**
column4: Lock in the current price for sunflower oil and basmati rice for at least 12–18 months, or use a commodity‑hedging instrument (e.g., futures or swaps) to cap the price.
column5: Eliminates price volatility and gives you predictable cost budgeting for all future catering events.
column6:
• Identify a reliable local supplier that can offer volume discounts.
• Negotiate a fixed‑price or “minimum‑purchase‑plus‑markup” contract with a 12‑month commitment.
• If the supplier can’t provide a fixed price, buy a futures contract on the relevant commodity exchange (or use a hedging service).
• Build a contingency clause to exit if the supplier breaches quality or delivery terms.

column4: Replace 30–40 % of sunflower oil with a cheaper alternative (e.g., canola or refined sunflower‑oil blend) and re‑evaluate rice portions in high‑volume dishes (biryani, steamed rice).
column5: Reduces direct ingredient cost without compromising flavour or client expectations.
column6:
• Pilot a test menu using canola oil in one‑day events; gather tasting data.
• Offer a “rice‑light” option for large groups (use 30 % less rice per plate, supplement with a side of mixed vegetables or dal).
• Train kitchen staff on the new cooking times and oil‑to‑rice ratios.
• Update the bill of materials and update the POS to reflect new cost structure.

column4: Adjust the pricing model so that the cost spike is absorbed proportionally across all catering orders, with a slightly higher surcharge for high‑volume or “special‑menu” events.
column5: Maintains profitability while keeping your price competitive for small orders.
column6:
• Re‑calculate your cost‑per‑plate figure and add a 5–7 % surcharge on events over 200 guests.
• Offer a “premium” package that includes the full rice‑and‑oil‑intensive dishes at a higher margin (e.g., premium biryani).
• Communicate the change transparently to long‑term clients and justify the price with a brief cost‑impact memo (highlighting the 10 % increase in key inputs).
• Monitor margin on each event and adjust the surcharge if needed.

column3: Roll‑out to all events & monitor margins

column1: - **Cost Savings:** Expected reduction of ~12 % on oil and rice expenses (depending on substitution efficiency).
- **Margin Protection:** Fixed‑price contract protects against future spikes; dynamic pricing keeps gross margin stable for larger events.
- **Customer Loyalty:** Transparent communication preserves trust, while menu tweaks keep dishes authentic.
Implement these three measures promptly to cushion Masala Boulevard against the 10 % cost spike and position the business for continued growth in Greater Manchester’s catering market."
